title: A Final Goodbye
content:
The mountains fell silent once again.

Sneha quietly looked at Siddu, waiting for him to continue.

A faint smile appeared on his face.

It wasn't the smile of happiness.

It was the smile of someone who had accepted the past.

________________________________________

"After that day..."

"I made a promise to myself."

"I would never fall in love again."

"I wouldn't chase anyone."

"I wouldn't expect anyone."

"I decided to stay away from every feeling that had once broken me."

"My only goal became my career."

"The pain didn't disappear overnight. Some nights were still difficult. But instead of letting it consume me, I slowly began pouring all my energy into my career."

The corners of Siddu's lips lifted slightly.

"Slowly..."

"My life began to change."

"I completed my graduation."

"I secured a great job."

"Then I completed my post-graduation as well."

"Later..."

"I received an excellent opportunity to work in Uttar Pradesh."

"My way of living changed completely."

"I became a different person."

"My parents were happier than they had ever been."

"When Kiran saw how much I had changed..."

"He smiled."

"He appreciated me for choosing my future over my past."

Siddu paused for a moment before continuing.

"But life has a strange way of bringing the past back to you..."

"No matter how far you run."

"One day..."

"My old Intermediate friends planned a reunion."

"They invited everyone."

"For a moment..."

"I was genuinely excited."

"It had been years since I had seen them."

"But the excitement disappeared the moment I learned that Shreya would be there."

"So..."

"I decided not to go."

Sneha listened quietly.

"But my father wouldn't let me avoid it."

"He looked at me and said..."

"'Go.'"

"'Meet your friends.'"

"'Meet Shreya.'"

"'Don't carry unfinished words in your heart for the rest of your life.'"

"'Say whatever you want to say.'"

"'Then move on completely.'"

Siddu smiled softly.

"So..."

"I went."

________________________________________

The reunion was filled with laughter.

Old memories returned.

Friends who hadn't seen each other for years embraced one another.

For a while...

It almost felt like nothing had changed.

Then...

She walked in.

Shreya.

The moment our eyes met...

She froze.

Shock spread across her face.

There was guilt in her eyes.

And...

There was fear.

She stood there without saying a word.

I quietly walked toward her.

She looked nervous.

As though she was expecting anger.

Or perhaps...

She thought I had come to question her.

I simply smiled.

"Don't be afraid."

"I haven't come here to hurt you."

"Not with my words."

"And certainly not with my actions."

"I just came to say..."

"Thank you."

She looked at me in confusion.

I continued.

"You're the reason I worked harder than I ever thought I could."

"Because of you..."

"I cracked JEE."

"Because of everything that happened..."

"I understood how unpredictable life could be."

"You taught me lessons that no classroom ever could."

"You unknowingly changed the direction of my life. If everything had gone the way I wanted, I might never have become the person I am today. The pain you gave me became the reason I discovered my own strength."

"So..."

"Thank you, Shreya."

"Thank you... for changing my life."

For a few moments...

Neither of us spoke.

She simply stood there, unable to respond.

I didn't wait for an answer.

Some conversations don't need one.

I gave her one final smile.

Turned around.

And quietly walked away.

Not because I was running from my past...

But because, for the very first time...

I had finally left it behind.
